en: I can choose between the present perfect and the past simple: the past simple when the time is finished, the present perfect when the experience still counts.
I can put two past events in order: the earlier one goes into the past perfect, had plus the third form.
I can talk about the future in three ways: the present continuous for a fixed arrangement, going to for an intention, will for a prediction or an on-the-spot decision.
I can build first and second conditionals: if with the present goes with will, if with the past goes with would.
I can build relative clauses with who, which and that, and leave the pronoun out when it is the object.
I can report what someone said: the tense steps back, and pronouns and time words shift with it.
I can build the passive in the present and the past: is or was plus the third form, with by for the doer where it matters.
I can draw conclusions with must, might and can't, and talk about obligation and advice with have to, don't have to and should.
I can choose whether -ing or to follows a verb: enjoy doing, decide to do, and the difference between stop doing and stop to do.
I can hold a long sentence together with linking words: although, however, so that, in order to and despite.
